content.thinking: I should confirm the repository still points to v2 given AI-3's note about re-enabling automatic sync, and double check that my proposed item actually answers CF-2 as required.

action_items.item: Set categoriser.model in deploy/values-production.yaml back to v1 until a deploy carries a fix for v2's input handling, so the repository says what should run.
Roll out categoriser model changes to a canary first, and stop the rollout automatically if the share of purchases categorised confidently falls below its baseline.
Page the on-call engineer when CategorisationConfidenceLow fires on io-shop.

causal_chain.step: Many purchases stopped being sorted confidently into a category. From {began}, the share of purchases categorised confidently fell from {series_before} to an average of {series_while_broken}, reaching {series_at_worst} at its worst. Requests did not fail more than they normally do.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision d268103129978816ce705c50c14cd42c7c5fe46e at {P1.1}. The metrics read across the hours after it held the confident share at its normal level until the onset at {began}.
A feature flag change. The flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the incident was acted on.
A change to the source code in the deploy. The deploy's diff touches only the model setting in the values file.

causal_chain.step: Every replica was running categoriser model v2 instead of v1. The deploy of revision 7c3ca00c7528df68d533f6e87acd4f23a55ab342 at {P2.1} changed categoriser.model from v1 to v2 in deploy/values-production.yaml and changed no other file. At {T10.1}, all {T10.2} replicas were read as running that revision. Rolling the deployment back brought the service off the incident's level, and that action was confirmed.

Under v2, capitalised words in purchase titles likely match nothing the model knows. Code-Fix read the code on main. In that code, v2 does not lowercase the words it receives and expects lowercase input, but `categorise` passes the title's words to it unchanged. So a title with no known all-lowercase word falls through to "General" with confident=False, and no request fails. Code-Fix did not read the running revision's own copy of this code.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The shop switched to a newer model for sorting purchases into categories, and that model likely fails to recognise capitalised words because it expects lower-case text that the shop never converts its product titles into.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that checked v2 against capitalised titles. Code-Fix read that the existing v2 tests covered only titles whose matching word was already lowercase.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test giving v2 capitalised titles would have failed before the model switch shipped, and the switch would not have reached production as it did.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The model switch reached every replica at once. No staged rollout and no check of how many purchases were categorised confidently was seen gating it before it served all traffic.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A canary watching the confident share would have shown the drop on a small part of the traffic and stopped the rollout before all purchases were affected.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator tied the drop to the model switch by reading the deploy's own diff. Argus checked the flag provider's history before acting.
Argus rolled back the deployment {T17.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed, {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that the rollback had brought the service off the incident's level.
Code-Fix proposed a fix as draft pull request #354, {T22.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged. No on-call incident was linked to the alert, so no person was brought in while the incident ran.
Code-Fix read the code on main rather than the revision that was running, and assumed the running revision's categorising code matched main's.

input.root_cause: Model v2 does not lowercase the words it is given. It expects lowercase input, because its training pipeline lowercased every title before its vocabulary was built. Code-Fix read on main that the shop's `categorise` passes the title's words to the model unchanged. So under v2, capitalised words match nothing, and a title with no known all-lowercase word falls through to "General" with confident=False.
input.still_at_risk: By Code-Fix's reading the shop still passes titles to the model without lowercasing them, so putting model v2 back into production before a deploy carries a fix would likely bring the drop in confident categorisation straight back.
input.symptom: Many purchases were no longer placed confidently into their proper category
